title: Session state file
description: The single source of truth for a running session. Written incrementally by the conductor after every stage, validated by scripts/validate_session.py (the executable form of this schema — keep the two in agreement). The narrative is stamped with its SHA-256 immediately after capture by deterministic code, never by the model, and reporting.reportable deliberately has no 'no' value: this tool never determines that a matter is unreportable.

user_confirmations.description: Verbatim user utterances backing consequential flags (e.g. mapping_notice). Weak evidence, honestly labeled: it makes silent flag-setting detectable, not lying impossible.

final_analysis_complete.description: True only after every queued independent incident is complete and the final combined reporting analysis has run. Assembly refuses an incident package until this is true.

position_type.description: Always national_security, DERIVED from scope rather than asked. Everyone this tool serves holds or is in process for eligibility for access to classified information. Public trust and low-risk positions do not carry clearances and are out of scope.

out_of_scope_acknowledged.description: Set when the user indicated they are not a clearance holder or applicant, was told this tool's rules may not be theirs, and chose to continue. Reportability is not determined for these sessions.

narrative.description: The user's verbatim intake account. Never rewritten — it is the candor baseline.

narrative_sha256.description: Set only by 'validate_session.py --stamp-narrative'. Validation fails if it no longer matches 'narrative'.

stage_log.description: Append-only. Stages may repeat (threads re-enter the pipeline); entries are never removed or rewritten.

stage_log_length_at_last_validate.description: Maintained by validate_session.py to detect log shrinkage. Do not set by hand.

incident_types.description: Applicable DISS Select Incident Type(s) values. Holder output only; multiple values may attach to one independent incident and one narrative.

future_update_topics.description: Tailored conditional developments that should prompt continued updates to the security office; never statements that the development already occurred.

incident_development.description: Gated before/during/after development record for this independent incident.

basis.description: Matched table entry ids from corpus/reporting/tables/, e.g. 'aci.travel.unofficial'. These are load-bearing twice: they are the citation for the obligation AND they select the event checklist that supplies the questions (corpus/checklists/events/). A determination with no basis leaves the gap analyst with a reportability answer and nothing to ask about.

no_new_obligation_identified.description: Set with reportable='consult_fso' when the user states this was disclosed in a prior investigation and is unchanged. Means: no NEW obligation identified on the user's account. Never a finding that the matter is unreportable — the tool cannot verify a prior disclosure.

prior_disclosure.description: Whether a past matter was already disclosed in a previous background investigation. Continuous reporting exists to surface NEW information; a matter already in the government's file does not need re-litigating. Rests entirely on the user's account, which the tool cannot verify.

what_changed.description: Required when status is disclosed_but_changed — the change IS the reportable matter.

scope_concern.description: Set when what they describe disclosing sounds narrower than what they have now described. Surfaced to the user, never resolved by the tool.
